title: CAD4TB on ultra-portable X-rays screened 94,694 people in eight Nigerian states and diagnosed 2,337 TB cases (2022)
summary: KNCV/USAID deployment Jan–Sep 2022: CAD4TB v7 screened 94,694 people in eight Nigerian states; 2,337 TB cases diagnosed, 97% treated
account: Under the Stop TB Partnership's Introducing New Tools Project, KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Nigeria and the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria, funded by USAID, deployed ten ultra-portable digital X-ray units with CAD4TB version 7 (threshold 50) for community active case finding in eight states (Katsina, Kano, Nasarawa, Benue, Delta, Cross River, Osun, Oyo) from January to September 2022 (day not given; first day of month used). Under a parallel algorithm, every client had both symptom and chest X-ray screening, and anyone positive on either (a CAD4TB score of 50 or above) was classified as presumptive TB and sent for Xpert testing and/or clinical assessment, so the software score was one of two gates to testing; of those diagnosed, 1,614 (69.1%) scored 50 or above and 723 (30.9%) scored below 50. The program screened 94,694 people aged four and over, identified 10,236 presumptive cases and diagnosed 2,337 TB cases (920 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,386 clinically diagnosed, 31 rifampicin-resistant), with 97.3% starting treatment and an average number needed to screen of 38. The paper's tables tally 2,481 diagnoses (986 bacteriologically confirmed, 1,466 clinically diagnosed, 29 rifampicin-resistant) with 2,414 (97.3%) started on treatment and derive the NNS of 38 from that tally; its text gives 2,337 diagnoses. A companion six-state analysis reported 85,910 screened, 1,915 diagnosed and 1,869 treated.
purpose: Triage chest X-rays to select presumptive TB cases for molecular testing during community active case finding.
system: CAD4TB computer-aided detection on ultra-portable digital chest X-ray
model_version: CAD4TB version 7, threshold score 50 or above
deployer: KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Nigeria and Institute of Human Virology Nigeria with the National TB and Leprosy Control Program, funded by USAID
taxonomy_note: Closest fit: diagnosis brought to hard-to-reach communities; yield and efficiency gains are organisational. General benefit without an event as instructed: aggregate yield, no individual outcome documented.

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: aggregate screening yield; the sources do not document any individual's outcome attributable to the software.
General benefit without an event: efficiency figures (NNS 38, NNT 4) are program aggregates without a discrete attributable event.
General benefit without an event: 2,337 diagnoses are an aggregate program result.

ai_role.statement: A parallel algorithm classified anyone positive on symptom screening or with a CAD4TB score of 50 or above as presumptive TB and sent them for Xpert testing and/or clinical assessment, so the AI score was one of two gates to testing, not the sole gate; 1,614 of the 2,337 diagnosed (69.1%) scored 50 or above and 723 (30.9%) scored below 50. The TB yield also depends on X-ray reach, Xpert availability and treatment linkage. Both papers are authored by implementing organizations (KNCV Nigeria, IHVN, USAID, NTBLCP), not the vendor.

paired_incident.title: Researchers find evidence of racial, gender, and socioeconomic bias in chest X-ray classifiers
paired_incident.basis: Chest X-ray classification systems, the same kind as CAD4TB, underdiagnosed economically vulnerable, female and Hispanic patients because of biased training data.
